subject: English
unit: Summer 1: Conflict poetry: power, memory and humanity
source: Written for english/y9 lesson 51 (Comparative connective bank and sentence-combining sheet (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 51: Grammar: comparative sentence structures. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.title: Sort into: Similarity / Difference / Qualification
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Similarity, Difference, Qualification.
blocks.answer: Similarity: similarly; likewise; both. Difference: whereas; in contrast; however. Qualification: to some extent; partly; although

head: Separate
Comparative
rows: Whereas the poem honours the men, the article blames the commanders.

model.title: Compare the poem and the article on the charge.

parts.text: Simple: Both texts describe the charge.
Contrast: The poem glorifies the men, whereas the article explains the error.
Qualified: Both admit a mistake, although Tennyson keeps the blame vague.
Evaluative: The article is more complete, yet the poem is more memorable

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Both texts admit a mistake, although Tennyson's vague 'Someone' protects the commanders, whereas the article names them.

keywords.def: a word or phrase that links ideas
joining two equal clauses with and, but, or
joining a less important clause to a main clause with whereas, although, while
a limit or condition on a statement: partly, to some extent

questions.q: Combine with 'whereas': 'Tennyson uses rhythm. The article uses dates.'
questions.a: Tennyson uses rhythm, whereas the article uses dates.

questions.q: Add a qualification: 'The poem criticises the commanders.'
questions.a: For example: 'To some extent the poem criticises the commanders, through the single line "Someone had blunder'd".'

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write four comparative sentences on the poem and the article, one each of similarity, difference, qualification and evaluation, each with evidence from both. Starter: 'Both texts...'
questions.a: Four accurate comparative sentences with embedded evidence from both texts.

questions.q: Extend: correct the error sheet (five separate-sentence comparisons to combine)
Stretch: write one sentence using 'while' to compare attitude
questions.a: For example: 'While Tennyson admires the men, the historian questions the leaders.'

questions.q: Which sentence qualifies the comparison most precisely?
options: Both texts are about a battle.
The poem is good and the article is good.
Both texts admit an error, although only the article names who made it.
questions.a: C) Both texts admit an error, although only the article names who made it.. 'although only' adds a precise limit to the similarity.

questions.q: Answer the ponder: how do you show precisely how two texts relate?
questions.a: For example: one sentence, two texts, a precise connective.
